title: Probability-of-Benefit Sensitivity Paths under Budgeted Violations of Cross-Trial Transition Invariance
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered subfield below the field floor; paper-score ceiling 7.0 < 7.4, salvageable=false; both math and decision panels pass after bounded cleanup.
gap_reasons: Its arbitrary-allocation results stop at an honest band, computable observation moduli, and a two-law lower bound; they do not establish a band attaining the Hellinger modulus or arbitrary-allocation minimax optimality, and the framing correctly leaves that issue open.

The contribution remains specialized to binary outcomes and a particular sensitivity-budget geometry, while the absence of empirical calibration leaves its practical importance demonstrated mainly by a constructed three-trial example.

proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the six-facet sharp endpoint profile, finite evaluator, target-specific initial coefficient, constructive witnesses, whole-path honest band, and comparable-allocation minimax rate. A maximality pass added allocation-specific observation moduli, a likelihood-region band, regular contrast, and a two-law lower bound; bounded cleanup then cleared both math and decision panels. The field-tier attempt ended because constant-factor expected-width adaptation to the Hellinger modulus under arbitrary allocations remains open, and the cold paper-score gate capped the sound result at subfield.
tldr: This paper gives a sharp sensitivity path around the Wu--Mao exact-invariance model: at \(\delta=0\) the theorem is an interior subclass of their exact class, while \(\delta>0\) defines a new free-center neighborhood. The path has six affine facets per trial, a finite balance dual, an \(O(m^3)\) rational critical-budget evaluator, explicit endpoint laws, and a proved at-most-\(2m\) target-specific initial coefficient. That coefficient is the exact initial slope of the sharp benefit interval: generic linear-program sensitivity and planar line arrangements motivate vertex search, while the theorem identifies the model-specific objective, its explicit candidate set, positivity under nonconstant baseline risks, and endpoint-attaining local path. Inference includes simultaneous whole-path coverage, exact product-arm-size Hellinger pseudometric and KL bridge moduli with finite-face computation, an allocation-aware regular contrast retaining the direct target-control contribution, an exact two-law lower bound, and a uniformly honest likelihood-region band. The sole allocation-aware open problem is uniform constant-factor expected-width adaptation to the same-radius Hellinger modulus through arbitrary allocations, face changes, and \(\nu\to0\), or a sharp impossibility and adaptation-penalty theorem.
gap: Wu--Mao's exact cross-trial transition restriction identifies binary joint potential outcomes but is a substantive cross-world equality, not a routine consequence of randomization; the closest work does not characterize the sharp probability-of-benefit path when actual trial transitions may differ under one shared free-center budget.
fill: The project derives the exact six-facet profile, finite dual and evaluator, target-specific local coefficient, attaining laws, joint-versus-separate phase diagram, and honest whole-path inference with a carefully delimited rate claim.
